newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government stock issue seen after budget.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government stock issue seen after budget.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government is likely to come into the local money market with a stock issue to help finance an 18-month budget to be unveiled on July 24, money market analysts said on Wednesday.
"Sources in the market reckon there will be a stock issue after the new budget is announced," one local money dealer said, adding however:
"But at this point in time we don't have any clear indication of volumes or the period (to maturity)."
But the analysts, who say borrowing at current rates would prove expensive, expect the government to wait until inflation, currently at 21.4 percent and interest rates averaging 25 percent subside.

"I would expect them to come in (with an issue) around September when rates will most likely have come down," one dealer told Reuters, saying at current rates, the market would probably be looking at a coupon of around 25 percent in the case of a five-year stock issue.

In its previous stock issue last December, the government only raised Z$146 million (U.S.$12.8 million) from an intended Z$1 billion ($87.9 million) and analysts blamed the flop on differences of opinion over the coupon rate. The government was offering 15 percent while the market wanted 19 percent.
Some analysts also say the government, wary of antagonising Western backers of its economic reform programme who have called on it to reduce its spending, will seek to keep borrowings to a minimum.

In an annual report of its operations for the 1996 financial year, the central Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe -- through which the government borrows from the market -- hinted that the government was buckling under the weight of its domestic debt.

"A disconcerting development has been the rise in interest on domestic government debt. Such payments impose an additional burden on the budget, at a time when government is striving to curb expenditure," central bank governor Leonard Tsumba said.

Latest official figures indicate that as of June 1996, the government's domestic debt stood at over Z$31.4 billion (U.S.$2.7 billion), almost twice the amount for the previous year. Long-term stock issues alone accounted for over Z$11 billion (U.S.$966.6 million)

Zimbabwe's external debt, which stood at Z$57.5 billion (U.S.$5.1 billion), is expected to rise to Z$60.9 (U.S.$5.4 billion) at the end of 1998, according to the London-based Economist Intelligence Unit. $1=Z$11.38
